question: Which of the following classical dance forms is associated with Hindustani Classical Music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India and is the principal classical dance form associated with Hindustani (North Indian) Classical Music. (कथक — हिंदुस्तानी शास्त्रीय संगीत)

 

• The word 'Kathak' is derived from 'Katha', meaning story, and the dancers who narrated stories were known as Kathakars.

 

• It flourished in the courts of North Indian kingdoms, especially Lucknow, Jaipur and Varanasi, giving rise to the Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras gharanas.

 

• Kathak is characterised by fast, rhythmic footwork (tatkar), spins (chakkars) and expressive storytelling (abhinaya), performed to Hindustani classical ragas and taals.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The eight classical dance forms of India are Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Odissi and Sattriya.

 

• Most other classical dance forms (Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, Mohiniyattam, Kathakali) are associated with Carnatic (South Indian) Classical Music.

 

NOTE

 

• Sattriya (Option 2): The classical dance of Assam, associated with Carnatic/regional Vaishnavite music traditions, not Hindustani music specifically.

 

• Mohiniyattam (Option 3): A classical dance of Kerala, associated with Carnatic music.

 

• Kathakali (Option 4): A classical dance-drama of Kerala, associated with Carnatic music.

question: Which of these is NOT an NGO involved in microfinance related activities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NABARD in Mumbai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development), headquartered in Mumbai, is an apex development financial institution set up by an Act of Parliament in 1982, not an NGO. (नाबार्ड — शीर्ष विकास वित्तीय संस्था, गैर-सरकारी संगठन नहीं)

 

• NABARD regulates and refinances rural financing institutions and pioneered the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme, but it is itself a statutory/government body, not a non-governmental organisation.

 

• MYRADA (Bangalore), SEWA (Ahmedabad) and ADITHI (Patna) are all genuine NGOs that pioneered microfinance and Self-Help Group models in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• SEWA (Self Employed Women's Association), founded by Ela Bhatt in 1972 in Ahmedabad, also runs the SEWA Bank, a cooperative bank for poor self-employed women.

 

• MYRADA, based in Bangalore, is credited with popularising the Self-Help Group (SHG) concept in India in the 1980s.

 

NOTE

 

• MYRADA in Bangalore (Option 1): A genuine NGO, pioneer of the SHG movement in Karnataka.

 

• SEWA in Ahmedabad (Option 3): A genuine NGO/trade union for women's microfinance and livelihood support.

 

• ADITHI in Patna (Option 4): A genuine NGO working on women's empowerment and microfinance in Bihar.

question: Which of the following committees had recommended to incorporate the Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swaran Singh Committee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Swaran Singh Committee, set up by the Congress government in 1976 under the chairmanship of Sardar Swaran Singh, recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution. (स्वर्ण सिंह समिति — मौलिक कर्तव्य)

 

• Based on its recommendations, the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 added a new Part IV-A containing Article 51A, which originally listed 10 Fundamental Duties (a 11th was added later by the 86th Amendment, 2002).

 

• The idea of Fundamental Duties was inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Soviet Union).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are enumerated in Article 51A of Part IV-A and are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts), like the Directive Principles of State Policy.

 

• The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 added the 11th Fundamental Duty regarding providing opportunities for education to children between 6-14 years.

 

NOTE

 

• Sarkaria Commission (Option 1): Set up in 1983 to examine and recommend changes in Centre-State relations, unrelated to Fundamental Duties.

 

• BN Patil Committee (Option 2): Not related to the recommendation of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution.

 

• Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (Option 3): Recommended the three-tier Panchayati Raj system in 1957, unrelated to Fundamental Duties.

question: Pratham Bank, the first Regional Rural Bank of India, had its Head Office in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prathama Bank, India's first Regional Rural Bank (RRB), was established on 2 October 1975 with its Head Office at Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh, sponsored by the Syndicate Bank. (प्रथमा बैंक — उत्तर प्रदेश)

 

• Regional Rural Banks were set up under the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976, following the recommendations of the Narasimham Committee (1975), to provide credit facilities to farmers, small entrepreneurs and rural labourers.

 

• RRBs are jointly owned by the Central Government (50%), the concerned State Government (15%) and a sponsor bank (35%).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Prathama Bank later merged with other RRBs in UP to form Prathama U.P. Gramin Bank.

 

• NABARD supervises and regulates the functioning of Regional Rural Banks in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajasthan (Option 1): Not the location of India's first RRB.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 2): Not the location of India's first RRB.

 

• Punjab (Option 3): Not the location of India's first RRB.

question: Which state has become the first state to launch a dedicated Semiconductor Policy in July 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gujarat became the first Indian state to launch a dedicated Semiconductor Policy (2022-27) in July 2022, aiming to attract chip manufacturing investment. (गुजरात — सेमीकंडक्टर नीति 2022-27)

 

• The policy offers incentives such as capital subsidy, electricity duty exemption, and reduced water tariffs to semiconductor and display fabrication units.

 

• Following this policy, Gujarat attracted India's first commercial semiconductor fabrication unit (Micron's ATMP facility at Sanand).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The India Semiconductor Mission (ISM), under MeitY, was launched in December 2021 with an outlay of ₹76,000 crore to develop a sustainable semiconductor ecosystem in India.

 

• Dholera Special Investment Region in Gujarat has emerged as a major hub for semiconductor fabrication plants.

 

NOTE

 

• Haryana (Option 1): Did not launch India's first dedicated Semiconductor Policy.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 2): Did not launch India's first dedicated Semiconductor Policy.

 

• Kerala (Option 3): Did not launch India's first dedicated Semiconductor Policy.

question: India won the Border-Gavaskar trophy 2023 by defeating ___________ and qualified for the World Test Championship Final.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Australia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Border-Gavaskar Trophy is contested between India and Australia; India won the 2022-23 series 2-1 at home in early 2023. (बॉर्डर-गावस्कर ट्रॉफी — भारत बनाम ऑस्ट्रेलिया)

 

• This series win helped India qualify for the final of the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) 2021-23, which was played against Australia at The Oval, London.

 

• The trophy is named after former captains Allan Border (Australia) and Sunil Gavaskar (India).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Australia won the WTC 2021-23 Final against India at The Oval in June 2023.

 

• India had earlier reached the first WTC Final (2019-21) as well, losing to New Zealand at Southampton.

 

NOTE

 

• Sri Lanka (Option 1): Not the opponent in the Border-Gavaskar Trophy.

 

• New Zealand (Option 2): Not the opponent in the Border-Gavaskar Trophy (New Zealand beat India in the first WTC final, 2021).

 

• South Africa (Option 4): Not the opponent in the Border-Gavaskar Trophy.

question: 'Uttar Ramcharita' was the composition of which of the following poets?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhavabhuti.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Uttar Ramcharita' (Uttararamacharita) is a famous Sanskrit play composed by Bhavabhuti, a court poet during the reign of the Kannauj ruler Yashovarman (8th century CE). (उत्तररामचरित — भवभूति)

 

• The play depicts the later life of Lord Rama after his return to Ayodhya, focusing on Sita's banishment and the family's reunion.

 

• Bhavabhuti also authored Malati-Madhava and Mahaviracharita.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhavabhuti is considered one of the greatest Sanskrit dramatists after Kalidasa.

 

• Sanskrit drama flourished under the patronage of various royal courts and reached its classical peak between the 4th and 8th centuries CE.

 

NOTE

 

• Jaideva (Option 2): Author of Gita Govinda, a lyrical poem on Lord Krishna and Radha.

 

• Hemchandra (Option 3): A Jain scholar-monk known for grammar and lexicography works like the Siddha-Hema-Shabdanushasana.

 

• Kalhan (Option 4): Author of Rajatarangini, a chronicle of the kings of Kashmir.

question: Which of the following statements is FALSE about the right to freedom of religion mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
option_1: It provides freedom to manage religious affairs.
option_3: It is mentioned in Articles 25 to 28.
option_4: It mentions that the state has its own religion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It mentions that the state has its own religion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India is a secular state, and the Constitution does not declare any state religion — this makes the given statement FALSE. (धर्म की स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार — भारत एक धर्मनिरपेक्ष राज्य)

 

• The Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28) guarantees every person the freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practise and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality and health.

 

• Article 26 provides freedom to manage religious affairs, Article 27 exempts a person from paying taxes for promotion of a particular religion, and Article 28 relates to freedom from attending religious instruction in certain educational institutions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The word 'secular' was added to the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

 

• Indian secularism follows the principle of equal respect for all religions, rather than a strict separation of state and religion.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (It provides freedom to manage religious affairs): This is TRUE — guaranteed under Article 26.

 

• Option 2 (It provides freedom of worship): This is TRUE — part of the freedom to profess, practise and propagate religion under Article 25.

 

• Option 3 (It is mentioned in Articles 25 to 28): This is TRUE — the Right to Freedom of Religion spans Articles 25-28.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding liquidity trap?

i. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely inelastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly elastic.

ii. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely elastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly inelastic.

iii. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely elastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly elastic.

iv. It is the point where speculative demand for money and the liquidity preference curves are not related.
option_4: Only Statements i and ii are correct
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only Statement iii is correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A liquidity trap is a Keynesian concept describing a situation where the speculative demand for money becomes infinitely elastic with respect to the interest rate, at a very low interest rate. (तरलता जाल — मुद्रा की सट्टा मांग अनंत लोचदार)

 

• At this point, people prefer to hold cash rather than invest in bonds because they expect interest rates to rise (and bond prices to fall) in the future, so the liquidity preference (LM) curve becomes perfectly elastic (horizontal).

 

• Statement iii is correct because it correctly describes both conditions — infinitely elastic speculative demand and a perfectly elastic liquidity preference curve — that together define the liquidity trap.

 

• In this state, monetary policy (changing money supply) becomes ineffective in influencing interest rates or investment, and only fiscal policy can stimulate the economy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The concept of liquidity trap was developed by John Maynard Keynes in his theory of liquidity preference.

 

• Liquidity traps are often cited in discussions of the Great Depression and periods of near-zero interest rates in modern economies like Japan.

 

NOTE

 

• Statement i: Incorrect — it wrongly states the speculative demand as 'infinitely inelastic', the opposite of the actual condition.

 

• Statement ii: Incorrect — it wrongly states the liquidity preference curve as 'perfectly inelastic', the opposite of the actual condition.

 

• Statement iv: Incorrect — the speculative demand for money and the liquidity preference curve are directly related, not unrelated.

question: ___________ won silver at the Fide World Blitz Chess Championship, becoming the first Indian woman to win a medal at the prestigious event in 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Koneru Humpy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Koneru Humpy won the silver medal in the Women's section of the FIDE World Blitz Chess Championship 2022, held in Almaty, Kazakhstan, becoming the first Indian woman to win a medal at this event. (कोनेरू हम्पी — फिडे विश्व ब्लिट्ज शतरंज चैंपियनशिप 2022)

 

• Koneru Humpy is a Grandmaster from Andhra Pradesh and a former Women's World Rapid Chess Champion (2019).

 

• She has consistently been one of the top-ranked women chess players in the world for over a decade.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Koneru Humpy became the second woman in history (after Judit Polgar) to cross a FIDE rating of 2600.

 

• She was awarded the Padma Shri in 2007 and the Arjuna Award in 2003.

 

NOTE

 

• Vantika Agrawal (Option 2): An Indian woman Grandmaster, but not the winner of this 2022 medal.

 

• Bhakti Kulkarni (Option 3): An Indian Woman Grandmaster, but not the winner of this 2022 medal.

 

• Rameshbabu Vaishali (Option 4): An Indian Woman Grandmaster (sister of R. Praggnanandhaa), but not the winner of this 2022 medal.

question: Which tunnel connects Manali to Lahaul-Spiti valley?
option_3: Dr Syama Prasad Mookerjee Road Tunnel
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atal Road Tunnel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Atal Tunnel (Atal Road Tunnel) connects Manali to the Lahaul-Spiti valley in Himachal Pradesh by passing under the Rohtang Pass. (अटल सुरंग — मनाली से लाहौल-स्पीति)

 

• It was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 3 October 2020 and is one of the longest highway tunnels above 10,000 feet in the world, at about 9.02 km.

 

• The tunnel provides all-weather connectivity to the Lahaul-Spiti valley, which was earlier cut off for nearly six months every year due to snow at Rohtang Pass.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Atal Tunnel was originally called the Rohtang Tunnel and was renamed after former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

 

• It reduces the road distance between Manali and Keylong by about 46 km.

 

NOTE

 

• Pir Panjal Railway Tunnel (Option 2): A railway tunnel in Jammu and Kashmir on the Banihal-Qazigund route, unrelated to Manali-Lahaul Spiti.

 

• Dr Syama Prasad Mookerjee Road Tunnel (Option 3): Located in Jammu and Kashmir (Chenani-Nashri tunnel), unrelated to Manali-Lahaul Spiti.

 

• Karbude Railway Tunnel (Option 4): A railway tunnel on the Konkan Railway route in Maharashtra, unrelated to Manali-Lahaul Spiti.

question: Which of the following states has the honour of being India's first carbon-free state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Himachal Pradesh declared itself India's first carbon-neutral (carbon-free) state in January 2020, at the Global Investors' Summit. (हिमाचल प्रदेश — भारत का पहला कार्बन-मुक्त राज्य)

 

• The state achieved this status largely due to its extensive forest cover and high dependence on clean hydropower rather than fossil fuels.

 

• Being carbon neutral means the state absorbs (through forests/sinks) at least as much carbon dioxide as it emits.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Himachal Pradesh is also known for hill stations such as Shimla, Manali and Dharamshala, and for apple cultivation.

 

• Sikkim is recognised separately as India's first fully organic state (2016).

 

NOTE

 

• Arunachal Pradesh (Option 1): Not recognised as India's first carbon-free state.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Not recognised as India's first carbon-free state.

 

• Kerala (Option 4): Not recognised as India's first carbon-free state.

question: What is the scientific name of the banyan tree, a large evergreen tree of Asia characterised by its trunk-like aerial roots?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ficus benghalensis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The banyan tree, India's National Tree, has the scientific (botanical) name Ficus benghalensis. (बरगद वृक्ष — फाइकस बेंगालेंसिस)

 

• It is characterised by its distinctive aerial prop roots, which descend from the branches and, upon reaching the soil, develop into woody trunk-like structures, allowing the tree canopy to spread over very large areas.

 

• The banyan tree belongs to the Moraceae (fig) family and is native to the Indian subcontinent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Great Banyan Tree in the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden, Howrah, is one of the widest-canopied trees in the world.

 

• The banyan tree was declared India's National Tree for its longevity and symbolic importance.

 

NOTE

 

• Gossypium herbaceum (Option 2): Scientific name of a species of cotton plant.

 

• Santalum album (Option 3): Scientific name of the Indian sandalwood tree.

 

• Ananas comosus (Option 4): Scientific name of the pineapple plant.

question: Cultivating large farms with moderately low inputs of labour and capital is referred to as ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is extensive cultivation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Extensive cultivation refers to farming practised over large tracts of land with relatively low inputs of labour and capital per unit area, relying more on the natural fertility of the soil. (विस्तृत कृषि — बड़े क्षेत्र, कम पूंजी/श्रम प्रति इकाई)

 

• It is common in regions with abundant land but limited labour, such as parts of the USA, Canada, Russia and Australia, where wheat and other grains are grown mechanically over large farms.

 

• Yield per hectare in extensive cultivation is typically lower, but total production can still be large because of the sheer area under cultivation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Its opposite, intensive cultivation, uses high inputs of labour and capital on relatively small landholdings, common in densely populated countries like India, Japan and China.

 

• Extensive cultivation is often associated with mechanised commercial farming.

 

NOTE

 

• Hybrid cultivation (Option 1): Refers to growing hybrid crop varieties, not a land-labour-capital classification.

 

• Intensive cultivation (Option 3): Involves high (not low) inputs of labour and capital on small landholdings — the opposite of the description given.

 

• Capitalist cultivation (Option 4): Not a standard agricultural classification term matching this description.

question: What was the percentage of women working in the primary sector of India as of 2011-2012?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 62.8%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per data for 2011-12, about 62.8% of working women in India were employed in the primary sector (agriculture and allied activities). (प्राथमिक क्षेत्र — महिला श्रमिकों का प्रतिशत, 2011-12)

 

• The primary sector comprises agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining and other activities directly using natural resources.

 

• A large share of India's female workforce continues to be concentrated in agriculture and allied rural activities, compared to the secondary and tertiary sectors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Women's participation in agriculture in India includes roles as cultivators as well as agricultural labourers.

 

• Over subsequent NSSO/PLFS rounds, the share of women employed in agriculture has shown a gradual declining trend as participation in the services sector rises.

 

NOTE

 

• 61% (Option 1): Not the figure recorded for 2011-12.

 

• 63.08% (Option 2): Not the figure recorded for 2011-12.

 

• 64.5% (Option 3): Not the figure recorded for 2011-12.

question: Padma Shri awardee of 2021, Kanaka Raju is associated with which of the following tribal folk dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gussadi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kanaka Raju, from Telangana, was conferred the Padma Shri in 2021 for his lifelong contribution to preserving the Gussadi (Gusadi) tribal folk dance, performed by the Gond tribe. (गुस्साडी नृत्य — कनक राजू)

 

• The Gussadi dance is a traditional tribal dance performed during the Dandari festival by the Gond community of the Adilabad region of Telangana.

 

• Kanaka Raju was noted as one of the earliest Adivasi (tribal) recipients of the Padma Shri for folk art preservation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Gussadi dancers wear elaborate headgear made of peacock feathers and other natural materials, and perform to traditional drumbeats.

 

• Several tribal and folk artists have been honoured with Padma awards in recent years to recognise India's grassroots cultural heritage.

 

NOTE

 

• Wancho (Option 2): Refers to the Wancho tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, not Kanaka Raju's dance form.

 

• Chalo (Option 3): Not the dance form associated with Kanaka Raju.

 

• Popir (Option 4): A folk dance of the Galo tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, not associated with Kanaka Raju.

question: Hardness of water is expressed in terms of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is ppm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The hardness of water is conventionally expressed in parts per million (ppm), typically as milligrams of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) equivalent per litre of water. (जल की कठोरता — ppm में व्यक्त)

 

• Water hardness is caused by dissolved calcium and magnesium salts (bicarbonates, sulphates, chlorides) in water.

 

• 1 ppm of hardness corresponds to 1 mg of CaCO₃ equivalent dissolved per litre (1,000,000 parts) of water.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Water is classified as temporary hard (due to bicarbonates, removable by boiling) or permanent hard (due to sulphates/chlorides, requiring chemical treatment).

 

• Hard water can be softened using methods like ion exchange, lime-soda process, or using washing soda (sodium carbonate).

 

NOTE

 

• mole (Option 1): A unit for the amount of substance, not used to express water hardness.

 

• molarity (Option 2): A unit for concentration of a solution (mol/L), not the conventional unit for water hardness.

 

• normality (Option 4): A unit for equivalent concentration, not the conventional unit for expressing water hardness.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common product offered by microfinance institutions in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Credit cards.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Microfinance Institutions (MFIs) in India primarily serve low-income and financially excluded populations by offering small collateral-free loans, savings products, and micro-insurance; credit cards are not a typical microfinance product. (सूक्ष्म वित्त संस्थाएं — क्रेडिट कार्ड सामान्यतः नहीं देतीं)

 

• MFIs mainly provide microloans (personal/business loans), basic savings accounts, and micro-insurance products tailored for low-income and rural clients, often through the SHG or Joint Liability Group model.

 

• Credit cards require formal credit assessment and are typically products of banks/NBFCs targeting a different customer segment, not the core offering of grassroots microfinance institutions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• MFIs in India are regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) as NBFC-MFIs.

 

• The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme, promoted by NABARD, is one of the largest microfinance models in the world.

 

NOTE

 

• Personal loans (Option 2): A common product offered by microfinance institutions.

 

• Insurance products (Option 3): Micro-insurance is a common product offered by microfinance institutions.

 

• Savings accounts (Option 4): A common product offered by microfinance institutions.

question: What is the minimum lane width in Swimming in metres?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.13.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per swimming pool regulations, the minimum lane width for a competitive swimming lane is 2.13 metres. (तैराकी में न्यूनतम लेन चौड़ाई — 2.13 मीटर)

 

• A standard competition swimming pool has 8 lanes (sometimes 10 including 2 empty outer lanes), each of the prescribed minimum width, along with a minimum pool length of 50 metres for Olympic-size pools.

 

• Lane width regulations ensure swimmers have adequate space and minimal interference from wave turbulence during competitive races.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Competitive swimming is governed internationally by World Aquatics (formerly FINA).

 

• Other pool specifications include a minimum water depth and specific requirements for starting blocks and lane ropes.

 

NOTE

 

• 2.10 (Option 1): Not the standard minimum lane width prescribed for swimming.

 

• 2.11 (Option 2): Not the standard minimum lane width prescribed for swimming.

 

• 2.12 (Option 3): Not the standard minimum lane width prescribed for swimming.

question: Which is the IUPAC group prefix of acyl halides compounds?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Halocarbonyl.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per IUPAC nomenclature, the substituent (prefix) name for the acyl halide (-CO-X) functional group is halocarbonyl. (एसिल हैलाइड — हैलोकार्बोनिल समूह)

 

• Acyl halides are derivatives of carboxylic acids in which the -OH group is replaced by a halogen atom (-X), giving the general formula R-CO-X.

 

• When named as a substituent prefix rather than a suffix, the -COX group is denoted using the prefix 'halocarbonyl' (e.g., chlorocarbonyl for -COCl).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• As a suffix, acyl halides are named using '-oyl halide' (e.g., ethanoyl chloride, commonly called acetyl chloride).

 

• Acyl halides are highly reactive and commonly used as acylating agents in organic synthesis.

 

NOTE

 

• Alkoxycarbonyl (Option 1): The IUPAC prefix for the -COOR (ester) group, not acyl halides.

 

• Carbamoyl (Option 2): The IUPAC prefix for the -CONH₂ (amide) group, not acyl halides.

 

• Cyano (Option 3): The IUPAC prefix for the -CN (nitrile) group, not acyl halides.

question: The Vernacular Press Act was enacted during the regime of which viceroy of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Lytton.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Vernacular Press Act, 1878 was enacted during the viceroyalty of Lord Lytton, to curb criticism of British policies in Indian-language newspapers. (वर्नाक्युलर प्रेस एक्ट, 1878 — लॉर्ड लिटन)

 

• The Act gave the government wide powers to confiscate the press and censor vernacular (Indian-language) newspapers that published material deemed 'seditious'.

 

• It was widely criticised as the 'Gagging Act' and was repealed in 1881 by Lord Ripon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lord Lytton also organised the grand Delhi Durbar of 1877 proclaiming Queen Victoria as Empress of India.

 

• Lord Ripon, who repealed the Vernacular Press Act, is also known for the Ripon Resolution of 1882 on local self-government.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Dalhousie (Option 1): Known for the Doctrine of Lapse, not the Vernacular Press Act.

 

• Lord Hastings (Option 2): Governor-General during the Anglo-Maratha and Anglo-Nepal Wars, not associated with the Vernacular Press Act.

 

• Lord Ripon (Option 3): Repealed the Vernacular Press Act in 1881; he did not enact it.

question: Tusu Parab is the harvest festival of which of the following Indian states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tusu Parab is a popular harvest festival celebrated primarily in Jharkhand (also in parts of West Bengal, Odisha and Assam), marking the end of the harvest season. (टुसू पर्व — झारखंड)

 

• The festival is celebrated by unmarried girls and women, who worship the goddess Tusu (a symbol of youth and beauty), and culminates on the last day of the Bengali month of Poush (mid-January), coinciding with Makar Sankranti.

 

• It involves folk songs called 'Tusu Gaan' and processions where the Tusu idol is immersed in a river.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major harvest/tribal festivals of Jharkhand include Sarhul and Karma.

 

• Tusu Parab is celebrated by various tribal and non-tribal communities in the Chhotanagpur plateau region.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat (Option 1): Not associated with Tusu Parab; known for festivals like Navratri and Uttarayan.

 

• Sikkim (Option 2): Not associated with Tusu Parab.

 

• Karnataka (Option 3): Not associated with Tusu Parab.

question: The photoelectric effect demonstrates which nature of light?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Particle nature.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The photoelectric effect — emission of electrons from a metal surface when light of sufficient frequency falls on it — demonstrates the particle (quantum/photon) nature of light. (प्रकाश विद्युत प्रभाव — प्रकाश की कण प्रकृति)

 

• Albert Einstein explained this effect in 1905 by proposing that light consists of discrete packets of energy called photons, for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921.

 

• The effect could not be explained by the classical wave theory of light, since electron emission depends on the frequency of light (not its intensity), which only a particle (photon) model could explain.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The photoelectric effect was first observed experimentally by Heinrich Hertz in 1887.

 

• Phenomena like interference and diffraction demonstrate the wave nature of light, giving rise to the concept of wave-particle duality.

 

NOTE

 

• Crystalline nature (Option 1): Not a recognised property/nature of light.

 

• Dual nature (Option 3): Light does exhibit wave-particle duality overall, but the photoelectric effect specifically demonstrates its particle nature.

 

• Wave nature (Option 4): The wave nature of light is demonstrated by phenomena such as interference and diffraction, not the photoelectric effect.

question: From which place did the Revolt of 1857 start?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meerut.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Revolt of 1857 began at Meerut on 10 May 1857, when sepoys mutinied over the issue of greased cartridges (rumoured to be coated with cow and pig fat) for the new Enfield rifles. (1857 का विद्रोह — मेरठ से शुरू)

 

• The mutineers marched to Delhi the next day and proclaimed the aged Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah II (Zafar) as the leader of the revolt.

 

• The revolt subsequently spread to other parts of North and Central India, including Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi and Bareilly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Key leaders of the Revolt of 1857 included Nana Sahib (Kanpur), Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi), Tantia Tope, and Begum Hazrat Mahal (Lucknow).

 

• The revolt led to the end of East India Company rule, and the British Crown took direct control of India through the Government of India Act, 1858.

 

NOTE

 

• Agra (Option 1): Witnessed events during the revolt but was not where it started.

 

• Kanpur (Option 3): An important centre of the revolt (led by Nana Sahib), but not where it started.

 

• Delhi (Option 4): Became the symbolic centre of the revolt after the mutineers arrived from Meerut, but the revolt did not start here.

• He has been honoured with several awards including the Padma Vibhushan (2000) for his contribution to Indian classical flute music.

 

• He is credited with popularising the bansuri as a solo classical instrument, moving it beyond its earlier folk associations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pandit Hari Prasad Chaurasia belongs to the Maihar gharana and has performed extensively with other legends such as Pandit Shivkumar Sharma.

 

• The bansuri is closely associated with Lord Krishna in Indian tradition.

 

NOTE
